claims.text: The target materials are CrFeCoNiX alloys, where X is Al, Si, or Mn, in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state.
Al addition promotes formation of a thin, coherent mixed oxide above 900 °C.
Si addition promotes formation of a thin, coherent mixed oxide above 900 °C.
The proposed protective oxide is a Cr-Al or Cr-Si spinel phase at the metal–oxide interface.
The proposed mixed oxide has low lattice mismatch with the alloy substrate.
The coherent Al- or Si-associated oxide grows slowly and uniformly.
A coherent oxide–metal interface accommodates thermal-expansion differences and relieves internal stresses.
The Al- or Si-associated oxide adheres strongly to the substrate.
Slow growth and strong adherence of the oxide inhibit further oxidation.
Stress accommodation by the coherent interface reduces crack initiation and subsequent spallation.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form less coherent and less adherent oxide scales.
The poorer oxide coherence associated with Mn is caused by higher diffusivity and volatility.
Mn-containing variants will exhibit faster oxide growth than Al- or Si-containing variants.
Mn-containing variants will exhibit more cracking and spallation than Al- or Si-containing variants.
High-temperature oxidation can culminate in catastrophic loss of specimen integrity near 900 °C.
The proposed comparison holds the processing and exposure conditions constant while changing X among Al, Si, and Mn.
The claimed operating boundary is sustained exposure at temperatures of at least 900 °C in air or another oxidative or corrosive environment.
The threshold Al or Si concentration needed for coherent oxide formation is unknown.
The quantitative improvement in thermal-stress accommodation from Al or Si is unknown.

Failure of Al- or Si-containing alloys to show significantly greater oxide coherence, slower growth, and fewer failure events than Mn-containing alloys under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
